title: Work
intro: Work is where the patterns show up most politely, and cost the most quietly. Answer about how you actually are at work, especially under pressure, with a manager, or in conflict with colleagues.

items.text: I can let others run things their way at work, even when I'd do it differently.
I need to be in control of projects to feel they'll go right.
I can stay in a tense meeting and keep engaging.
When feedback gets personal, I shut down or go defensive.
I own it when something I did goes wrong at work.
When a project fails, I can always point to why it wasn't down to me.
I notice how my tone lands with colleagues while I'm speaking.
People have told me I come across harsher than I mean to.
I can disappoint a colleague without over-explaining.
I write long messages to make sure nobody's annoyed with me.
I'm fine when my manager doesn't check in for a while.
If my manager is short with me, I worry about it all day.
Under deadline pressure, I can still think clearly.
When work piles up, I panic and can't prioritise.
I can say no to extra work when I'm at capacity.
I take on more than I can handle so I don't let people down.
I feel like the same person at work and at home.
I keep a calm face at work while I'm stressed underneath.
I do what I say I'll do at work.
I bend my values to fit in or get ahead.
Colleagues know what to expect from me.
My mood at work changes how I treat people.
I can look honestly at my own performance.
I avoid feedback that might show I'm not doing well.
I know what I want from my work and I'm moving towards it.
I throw myself into new roles or projects, then lose interest fast.
I can spot the situations at work that set me off.
I keep ending up in the same clashes with different people.
When I'm at my limit at work, I step away before I snap.
I've sent messages or said things at work in the heat of the moment I regretted.
I've changed a work habit that used to cause me trouble.
I burn out, recover, then do it all again.

narc.title: The controller
narc.text: At work you contract under pressure: you take control, defend your position and shut down when it gets personal. You get things done, but people may stop telling you things.

empath.title: The over-giver
empath.text: At work you expand under pressure: you over-explain, take on too much and worry about how you're seen. People rely on you, and your own capacity disappears.

loop.title: Boom and burnout
loop.text: You swing between holding it all tightly and giving everything away. The red codes show where the swing starts.

mixed.title: Mostly steady at work
mixed.text: No strong pull either way. A few codes show where work pressure tips you; fix those first.

zero.title: Grounded at work
zero.text: You stay steady at work more often than not. Watch the amber codes in busy seasons.
